definition: Moving a futures position or a continuous series from the expiring contract to the next, when the next contract's volume (or open interest) passes the expiring one's, or on a set date.
boundaries: Never the carry charge: the FX and CFD daily swap is rollover-swap-cost@1. The roll rule is 0 for calendar, 1 for volume and 2 for open_interest, QML's roll-rule words; the instrument record's root, expiry and rolls_to name the contracts, and the unit names its root and its rule. Some index CFDs are dated and expire instead of rolling.
recognition: Volume moving to September in the June contract's last week reads as the roll.

class_meanings.fx: none: 'rollover' on FX is the daily swap charge, rollover-swap-cost@1.
class_meanings.metal: none for spot CFDs; the swap is rollover-swap-cost@1.
class_meanings.index_cfd: Cash CFDs never roll; dated CFDs expire and are never rolled by the broker.
class_meanings.commodity_cfd: The broker rolls the underlying future and adjusts the CFD.
class_meanings.future: From the expiring to the next contract, by volume, open interest or date.

sources.quote: When the September contract has more volume than the June contract
Futures: moving from the expiring to the next contract.
